verdict.rationale: The evidence shows Slack publishing its own official MCP server so external MCP clients (Claude, agents, etc.) can call Slack's tools (search, send messages, canvases, lists) — this is Slack acting as an MCP server/provider, not as a client that itself ingests third-party MCP servers to gain their tools. There is no evidence that Slack (e.g., Slackbot or its AI agent features) lets a user plug in arbitrary external MCP servers so Slack's own AI can use those tools. missing for 10: any documentation of Slack's AI/agent features consuming external MCP servers as a client, configuration UI/API for adding MCP server URLs to Slackbot, and community/hands-on confirmation of such client-side MCP support.
